column1: # internal/tui intended package graph (Session 1.6, Phase 0).
# One row per target sub-package. Columns: package, layer, depends_on.
# `depends_on` is the complete set of sibling packages that package may import,
# comma-separated, or `-` for none. It is a whitelist, not a floor: an import
# absent from the row is a violation even when the target sits lower.
# This is the graph in context.md made mechanical. `tui_layer_fitness_test.go`
# reads it and fails on any real import under internal/tui that the table does
# not allow, so an upward or sideways edge is a red test rather than prose.
# `scripts/tui_package_assignments.tsv` says which file lands in which package
# and must agree with the `layer` column here.
# Layers are advisory to a reader and load-bearing to the table's own audit: a
# package may only name a dependency in the same layer or below, and the
# declared graph must be acyclic.
# Where this table is stricter than context.md, and why:
#   - `keymap` is absent from context.md's diagram but is a real L0 package with
#     sixteen production consumers today. It is named explicitly by `chrome`,
#     `listsurface`, `help`, every L7 surface and the shell, because Go imports
#     are not transitive: a file that names keymap.Binding needs the edge even
#     when its package already reaches keymap through chrome.
#   - context.md writes L7's lower dependencies as `...`. That ellipsis is
#     spelled out here as the full L0-L6 set; the L7-internal edges
#     (`projecthub -> notes`, `outliner -> taskform, taskdetail, lens,
#     projecthub`) are what keep the layer one-directional.
#   - `conflict` is a sibling of `outliner`, not a dependency of it. `gc`
#     browses conflict bundles as a shell-owned overlay, so the shell holds
#     that edge.
#   - Five edges run inside L0, and all of them are the same shape: an L0
#     package needs a bare vocabulary another L0 package owns, and threading the
#     value in from every call site would be a redesign Phase 1 does not do.
#     None can close a cycle: `theme`, `taskref`, and `presentation` depend on
#     nothing, and `textfit` reaches only `theme`, so no target of an L0 edge
#     can reach back to its source.
#   - `status -> presentation` is the second, added in Session 2.6.
#     `ViewStatusClearMsg` names the view whose status line it clears, so the
#     message carries a `presentation.PresentationID` field. That is why
#     `presentation` was split out as its own L0 package in the first place —
#     context.md calls the bare enum load-bearing below `operation`, and the
#     same argument reaches one layer further down.
#   - `pulse -> theme,textfit,taskref` are the last three, added in Session 2.7.
#     The workspace pulse and the operational title row it feeds are rendered
#     output, so `theme` styles every component and `textfit` truncates the
#     identity region; `taskref` is the project-qualified planning identity the
#     Today count is deduplicated by. All three are vocabulary the counter and
#     the row are written in rather than values a caller could supply.
#   - `query -> theme,pulse,chrome` were added in Session 2.13, and they are the
#     same argument one layer up. Three of `query`'s files render rather than
#     decide: `RenderFilterBadge` paints the facet chips through
#     `theme.FilterBadgeStyle` into `pulse.OperationalTitleBadge`,
#     `TagInfo.ListSurfacePrimaryStyle` resolves `theme.TagChipStyle` on the
#     payload so a retained selector cannot re-mint a plain row, and
#     `FormatDueDate`/`FormatRecencyChip` classify a due date through
#     `chrome.ClassifyDueDate`. The alternative is a fourth spelling of a due
#     date and a second tag-color authority, both of which CLAUDE.md forbids
#     outright. None can close a cycle: `chrome` names `theme,textfit,pulse,
#     taskref,keymap` and no L0 or L1 package reaches `query`.
#   - `operation -> query` was added in Session 2.14, and it is the same shape
#     one layer up again. `ValueProviderID.AcceptsPresetValue` refuses a key
#     binding whose preset names a spelling no picker row writes, and the due
#     and dependency facet rows are canonical tokens `query` owns. CLAUDE.md
#     states that refusal as a rule, so the check has to read the vocabulary
#     rather than a copy of it, and it runs where a strategy is registered
#     rather than where a key is pressed. It cannot close a cycle: `query` names
#     `theme,pulse,taskref,chrome,grammar` and none of those reaches `operation`.
#   - `listsurface -> presentation` was added in the same session, for
#     ListCategoryID. The operation manifest names a list category on every
#     entry so an action sheet can group what it lists, which puts the identity
#     below the surface that owns the concept; `presentation` is where the bare
#     enum lives and `listsurface` spells it through an alias, so this edge
#     carries one declaration and no behavior.
#   - `route -> theme` was added in Session 2.17. `view_accent.go` was assigned
#     to `route`, not `theme`, back in Session 2.1 precisely because the accent
#     category is navigation identity: `presentationAccentCategory` reads a
#     PresentationID and `accentColorForCategory` resolves the four
#     `theme.Accent*` variables it names. Only the resolution step is theme's,
#     and it is four constant reads, so the edge carries no rendering. It cannot
#     close a cycle: `theme` is L0 and depends on nothing.
#   - `listsurface -> taskref,query,status,pulse` were added in Session 2.19,
#     when the package was extracted and the row could be read off real imports
#     rather than predicted. All four are vocabulary the moved files are written
#     in: `MultiSelectState`, the parent selector and the tag selector hold and
#     compare `taskref.TaskIdentity` because a selection is project-qualified;
#     `tag_selector.go`, `tag_add_shared.go` and `list_surface_sources.go` name
#     `query.TagInfo` and `query.BuildProjectTagList` so a retained tag row
#     carries the one chip style CLAUDE.md allows, and read a search query's
#     `Raw`/`Normalized`/`Terms`; `shared_navigation.go` and
#     `contextual_action_sheet.go` emit `status.StatusMsg` and time the cursor
#     flash by `status.CursorFlashTimeout`; and `base_view.go` embeds
#     `pulse.WorkspacePulseState` as the bottom of the three-level embed chain.
#     None can close a cycle: `taskref`, `status` and `pulse` are L0 and
#     `query` is L2, and no package below L5 reaches `listsurface`.
#   - `help -> route,theme,textfit,pulse` were added and `help -> grammar`
#     removed in Session 2.21, when the package was extracted and its row could
#     be read off real imports rather than predicted. The viewer is a full-screen
#     view, so it satisfies `route.View`, embeds `pulse.WorkspacePulseState`
#     through the shared base, styles every column with `theme`, and wraps a
#     description with `textfit`. The removed edge was a name collision:
#     `help_grammar.go` projects the capture sigils into help rows, but it reads
#     them from `internal/textgrammar`, the parser package, and never from
#     `internal/tui/grammar`, the surface package this column names. None of the
#     four can close a cycle: `theme`, `textfit` and `pulse` are L0 and `route`
#     is L4, and no package below L6 reaches `help`.
#   - `notes` lost `taskref,pulse,coordinator,grammar,query` in Session 2.22,
#     when the package was extracted and its row could be read off real imports
#     rather than predicted. Notes are location-qualified, never task-qualified,
#     so no file names `taskref.TaskIdentity`; the manager holds no task and
#     never asks `coordinator` a date question, writes no capture grammar, and
#     compiles no facet, so `grammar` and `query` go unread too. `pulse` is
#     reached only through the base view it embeds, and Go imports are not
#     transitive in the other direction: an edge nothing spells is a dependency
#     nothing has. What remains is what a full-screen list surface is written
#     in -- `route.View` and `presentation.PresentationID` for navigation,
#     `listsurface` for the base and the preview, `operation` for the strategy
#     and the descriptors, `chrome`/`theme`/`textfit` for the render,
#     `keymap.Binding` for the help projection, `status` for the notice, and
#     `help` because `?` raises the viewer from this surface. Removing five
#     edges can close no cycle.
#   - `textfit -> theme` is the first edge inside L0, added in Session 2.3 when
#     the package was extracted. context.md gives `textfit` "Markdown,
#     highlighting" and both are inherently styled: `markdown.go` picks the
#     dark or light glamour style from `theme.ActiveThemeName` and
#     `highlight.go` paints matched runes with `theme.HighlightStyle`. The
#     alternative was passing both in from six call sites, which is a redesign
#     Phase 1 does not do. It is safe by construction: `theme` is L0 and
#     depends on nothing, so this edge can never close a cycle.
